FOREX-Dollar gains traction as Fed speakers warn of risks from inflation Reuters | Updated: 11-11-2026 06:20 IST | Created: 11-11-2026 06:20 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The dollar held gains near a two-week high in early Asian trade on Wednesday as a hotter-than-expected inflation report and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials fuelled bets the central bank will raise rates next month. The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was steady at 102.22, closing in on its highest level since October 28. The gauge traded up 0.5% on Tuesday after data showed US consumer prices increased by more than expected in October amid higher costs for food and accommodation. "The rates market isn't simply pricing another hike," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group Ltd in Melbourne. "It's questioning how restrictive US monetary policy may ultimately need to become, and that's a far more consequential debate for risk assets." The dollar held onto its gains against its major peers in early Asian trade. The euro and the British pound were flat at $1.1168 and $1.3345, respectively. Against the yen , the US dollar was unchanged at 158.715 yen. The Australian dollar was up 0.1% at $0.6870, edging back from a seven-month low, while the New Zealand dollar was flat at $0.5605. Comments from voting members of the Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee signalling unease over high inflation have firmed expectations for further rate hikes, prompting traders to all but abandon bets that the US central bank will stand pat at its next policy meeting, which concludes on December 9. Fed funds futures now imply a 91.9% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month, up from 84% a day earlier, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. Markets have fully priced out the possibility of a pause and see a 9.1% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move, while assigning better-than-even odds to a second hike in January. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond was up 13.8 basis points at 4.996%. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin was down 0.3% at $73,566.45 while ether was 0.5% lower at $2,044.61, both trading near three-month lows.

US Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, NYT reports Reuters | Updated: 11-11-2026 06:16 IST | Created: 11-11-2026 06:16 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently moved out of his home and onto a military base after Iranian threats against his life, the New York Times reported on Tuesday, citing sources with knowledge of the matter. Iran has ramped up efforts to target US personnel, and lethal plots by Tehran against American citizens have reached "advanced stages", a senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month. The newspaper reported that the severity of the threats to Bessent was not immediately clear. Iran has previously denied plotting to attack officials and people on US soil. The newspaper reported that US officials have noted that Iran's ability to carry out large-scale attacks in the US and other territories overseas is limited. The US Treasury Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Bessent has been the face of Washington's economic pressure campaign against Tehran during the course of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon during the war have killed thousands and displaced millions. American and Israeli attacks have also killed top Iranian officials, including late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

item.content:encoded:
Kennedy family tries to stop Trump's Washington arch  Reuters | Updated: 11-11-2026 06:11 IST | Created: 11-11-2026 06:11 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Several members of the Kennedy family, one of America's most famous political dynasties, filed on Tuesday to join a court case aimed at stopping President Donald Trump from building a proposed triumphal arch in Washington, saying it would obstruct views and cast shadows over their relatives' grave sites. The 250-foot (76-meter) arch, shown in a rendering to include a flame held by a 60-foot gold winged female figure and flanked by gold flying eagles, would be situated across the Potomac River from the Lincoln Memorial on a highway roundabout near the entrance to the Arlington National Cemetery. A judge has already issued a temporary order blocking construction through November 19 as she considers whether to issue a preliminary injunction. The arch "will permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sight lines to the existing grave sites and memorials established in the Kennedy family’s honor at Arlington National Cemetery, as well as to the memorials of hundreds of thousands of fallen American heroes," the filing said. The Kennedy family is one of the most prolific political dynasties in US history, notably including former President John F. Kennedy. Trump's health secretary is Robert F. Kennedy Jr., nephew to the assassinated former president. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters. The Trump administration contends Congress approved the arch more than 100 years ago when it also authorized construction of a bridge across the Potomac River. It has said that the arch would honor veterans. Numerous Democrats in Congress have vowed to block construction once they take control in January, after winning November's midterm elections. (Additional reporting by David Shepardson; editing by Michelle Nichols )

item.content:encoded:
US confident Russian diesel cargo off US coast will sell in global market Reuters | Updated: 11-11-2026 01:45 IST | Created: 11-11-2026 01:45 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

President Donald Trump's energy chief said on Tuesday the US was confident that the first cargo of Russian diesel headed for the US would eventually get sold in the global market despite the tanker carrying it coming to a halt recently. Shipping data showed on Tuesday that the Agioi Fanendes has come to a halt off the US east coast. The haltfollowed warnings by a US governor and lawmakers about the legality of the ship's landing in the US. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, asked whether he was concerned that the vessel, which had originally signalled it was headed to New York, had been turned away, said he had no worries. "Not at all. No, it'll go to another port," Wright told reporters in New Orleans. "We just want that diesel going into the world markets." President Donald Trump last month announced a surprise deal with Moscow to import diesel from Russia to help lower prices at the pumps ahead of this month's US midterm elections. New Jersey's Democratic Governor Mikie Sherrill this month warned local port officials and terminal operators against accepting Russian diesel, saying those shipments would break federal law. Sherrill said importing Russian diesel could expose businesses and individuals using New Jersey ports to harsh civil and criminal penalties. Senators from both parties said last month that US law bars imports of energy from Russia until it ends aggression against Ukraine. The Malta-flagged tanker was loaded with 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel in Russia's Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22, LSEG shipping data showed, with an expected delivery date of November 7. But Eastmed, the Greece-based company which manages the tanker, said a week later that the vessel was proceeding awaiting orders and that a port of discharge had not yet been nominated or finalised. "Nothing has changed regarding the vessel's destination, she is still awaiting orders," Greece-based vessel manager Eastmed told Reuters on Tuesday. Vessels may change their declared destination or revert to "for orders" status more than once during a voyage when a prospective deal falls through, plans change or the operator does not wish to declare its intended destination. Other tankers carrying Russian diesel which had signalled the US Atlantic Coast as their destination later altered course, shipping data showed. RUSSIAN IMPORTS BANNED IN 2022 Former President Joe Biden had imposed a ban on US imports of Russian oil and petroleum products in 2022 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Trump in approving the deal last month waived parts of a new US sanctions law on Moscow and said Russia would immediately export 300,000 tons, or 2.25 million barrels, to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter". Ellie Valencia, a senior analyst at Vortexa, said the ship's speed had come down from 10 knots several days ago to about 2 knots currently. "What you can interpret from the speed is directly related to the status of the ship which is "FOR ORDERS", most likely meaning that it doesn’t yet have a specific buyer," Valencia said.
